nodes.description: Address of the current contract owner; set to msg.sender in the constructor and used by the onlyOwner authorization checks.
Pending owner address written by transferOwnership and promoted to owner in acceptOwnership.
ERC20 token symbol state variable, set to "GAIN" in the constructor.
ERC20 token name state variable, set to "GAMEINVEST.IO" in the constructor.
ERC20 decimal precision state variable, set to 18 in the constructor.
Total minted supply, assigned in the constructor and read by totalSupply().
Mapping of holder address to token balance, mutated by transfer, transferFrom and the constructor.
Nested mapping owner => spender => amount, used by approve, transferFrom, allowance and approveAndCall.
Safe addition helper that performs a + b and requires c >= a to detect overflow.
Safe subtraction helper that requires b <= a then computes a - b.
Safe multiplication helper that computes a * b and requires a == 0 || c / a == b.
Safe division helper that requires b > 0 then computes a / b.
Owned constructor that assigns msg.sender as the initial owner.
onlyOwner function that stages a new owner into newOwner.
Two-step ownership acceptance; requires msg.sender == newOwner and moves newOwner into owner.
Token constructor initializing metadata, total supply, owner and the owner's balance.
Returns _totalSupply minus balances[address(0)].
Returns the balance of the given tokenOwner.
Transfers tokens from msg.sender to a recipient using safeSub/safeAdd balance updates.
Sets allowed[msg.sender][spender] to tokens without any double-spend checks.
Transfers tokens from a pre-approved owner account, decrementing balances and allowance.
Returns the remaining allowance of spender over tokenOwner.
Approves a spender and then performs an external call to its receiveApproval function.
Payable fallback function that unconditionally reverts, rejecting plain Ether transfers.
onlyOwner rescue function that performs an external call to an arbitrary ERC20 contract.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership assignment, authorization checks and balance/allowance indexing.
External call to ApproveAndCallFallBack(spender).receiveApproval(msg.sender, tokens, this, data) with an attacker-controlled target address.
External call ERC20Interface(tokenAddress).transfer(owner, tokens) to a fully user-supplied contract address.
Addition a + b in safeAdd; relies on a post-hoc require(c >= a) to guard overflow.
Subtraction a - b in safeSub; guarded only by require(b <= a).
Multiplication a * b in safeMul; guarded by require(a == 0 || c / a == b).
Division a / b in safeDiv; guarded by require(b > 0).
Abstract callback function implemented by an untrusted spender contract invoked by approveAndCall.
Constant expression (980000000) * (10 ** 18) used to compute the initial total supply.

Dividend parameter of SafeMath.safeDiv.

Return value holding the quotient in safeDiv.
Candidate new owner address passed to Owned.transferOwnership.
Address whose token balance is queried in balanceOf.
Recipient address of the transfer function.
Amount of tokens moved by the transfer function.
Address granted the allowance in approve.
Allowance amount granted in approve.
Source account debited in transferFrom.
Destination account credited in transferFrom.
Amount of tokens moved in transferFrom.
Owner whose allowance is inspected in allowance.
Spender whose remaining allowance is inspected in allowance.
Contract address that is approved and then called by approveAndCall.
Allowance amount granted and forwarded by approveAndCall.
Arbitrary calldata forwarded to the spender's receiveApproval.
Arbitrary ERC20 contract address whose transfer is invoked by transferAnyERC20Token.
Amount of foreign tokens moved by transferAnyERC20Token.

edges.reason: Owned constructor writes msg.sender into the owner state variable, establishing privileged control.
Untrusted msg.sender is the value stored in owner, so ownership is caller-controlled.
Owned constructor reads the untrusted msg.sender value.
transferOwnership consumes the _newOwner parameter.
transferOwnership writes the newOwner state variable.
onlyOwner modifier on transferOwnership compares untrusted msg.sender against owner.
onlyOwner authorization uses the owner state variable as reference.
acceptOwnership requires the untrusted msg.sender to equal newOwner.
acceptOwnership checks the newOwner state variable before promotion.
acceptOwnership promotes newOwner into the owner state variable.
Constructor initializes the symbol state variable.
Constructor initializes the name state variable.
Constructor initializes the decimals state variable.
Constructor assigns the initial _totalSupply.
Constructor mints the total supply into balances[owner].
Token constructor reassigns the owner state variable to msg.sender.
Token constructor reads the untrusted msg.sender to become owner.
totalSupply reads the _totalSupply state variable.
totalSupply subtracts balances[address(0)] from the stored supply.
balanceOf consumes the tokenOwner parameter.
balanceOf reads the balances mapping.
transfer consumes the recipient parameter to.
transfer consumes the tokens amount parameter.
transfer reads and writes the balances mapping for sender and recipient.
transfer debits balances[msg.sender], making the caller the implicit spender.
transfer invokes SafeMath.safeSub on the sender balance.
transfer invokes SafeMath.safeAdd on the recipient balance.
Balance decrement in transfer flows through the safeSub subtraction operation.
Balance increment in transfer flows through the safeAdd addition operation.
approve consumes the spender parameter.
approve consumes the tokens allowance parameter.
approve writes the allowed nested mapping.
approve sets allowed[msg.sender][spender] using the untrusted caller address.
transferFrom consumes the source account parameter from.
transferFrom consumes the destination parameter to.
transferFrom consumes the tokens amount parameter.
transferFrom decrements allowed[from][msg.sender], authorizing via the untrusted caller.
transferFrom reads and writes the allowed allowance mapping.
transferFrom updates balances for the from and to accounts.
transferFrom invokes SafeMath.safeSub on balance and allowance.
transferFrom invokes SafeMath.safeAdd on the destination balance.
Allowance and balance decrements in transferFrom flow through safeSub.
Destination balance increment in transferFrom flows through safeAdd.
allowance consumes the tokenOwner parameter.
allowance consumes the spender parameter.
allowance reads the allowed nested mapping.
approveAndCall consumes the spender address parameter.
approveAndCall consumes the tokens parameter forwarded to the callee.
approveAndCall forwards the arbitrary data parameter to the callee.
approveAndCall writes the allowed allowance mapping.
approveAndCall uses msg.sender both as allowance owner and as the from argument of the external call.
approveAndCall performs an external call to the user-supplied spender contract.
The external call invokes receiveApproval on the untrusted spender implementation.
The untrusted receiveApproval callback can re-enter the token contract during approveAndCall.
transferAnyERC20Token consumes the arbitrary tokenAddress parameter.
transferAnyERC20Token consumes the tokens amount parameter.
onlyOwner modifier on transferAnyERC20Token checks the untrusted msg.sender.
transferAnyERC20Token reads the owner state variable as the transfer beneficiary.
transferAnyERC20Token performs an external call into a fully user-controlled contract address.
The arbitrary ERC20 contract can call back into the token while the external call is pending.
safeAdd executes the a + b addition before the overflow require check.
safeSub executes the a - b subtraction after requiring b <= a.
safeMul executes the a * b multiplication guarded by c / a == b.
safeDiv executes the a / b division guarded by require(b > 0).
Constructor computes the initial supply with a multiplication expression.
safeAdd reads its first operand parameter a.
safeAdd reads its second operand parameter b.
safeAdd writes its return value c.
safeSub reads its minuend parameter a.
safeSub reads its subtrahend parameter b.
safeSub writes its return value c.
safeMul reads its first factor parameter a.
safeMul reads its second factor parameter b.
safeMul writes its return value c.
safeDiv reads its dividend parameter a.
safeDiv reads its divisor parameter b.
safeDiv writes its return value c.
